We propose a Prompt Expansion model that takes a user text query as input and returns N text prompts ... we train a PaLM 2 language model ... to map query text to expanded prompt text.

The Prompt Expansion model takes a text query as input and outputs a set of expanded text prompts that are optimized such that when passed to a text-to-image model, they generate a wider variety of appealing images.
outputs: expanded text prompts for image generation

quote: We use 3 metrics to evaluate the images generated from the prompts returned by the models described above. For aesthetics, we use MUSIQ ... For diversity, we use the variance (σ p ) of the COCA image embeddings ... For text-image alignment, we use the cosine similarity ...

We use MUSIQ for aesthetic scores, the variance (σp) of the COCA image embeddings for diversity, and the cosine similarity between COCA text embeddings of the query and the generated image for text‑image alignment.

We use 3 metrics to evaluate the images generated from the prompts returned by the models described above. For aesthetics, we use MUSIQ... For diversity, we use the variance (σ p ) of the COCA image embeddings of the generated images. For text-image alignment, we use the cosine similarity between the COCA text embeddings of the query text against the COCA image embeddings of the generated image, similar to CLIP-score.

We perform a side-by-side (SxS) evaluation task: we show raters a pair of images side by side for a given text query ... Each SxS evaluation is conducted for 2 criteria: aesthetic preference and text-image alignment.

We perform a side‑by‑side (SxS) evaluation task, where we show raters a pair of images ... ask the rater to pick the best one. Raters are instructed to evaluate aesthetics ... and text‑image alignment.

We perform a side-by-side (SxS) evaluation task: we show raters a pair of images side by side for a given text query, where each image is generated by a prompt from one PE model or the other, and ask the rater to pick the best one.
guideline: For aesthetics: 'Which image do you personally prefer?' (based on aesthetic, stylistic or compositional qualities). For text-image alignment: 'Which image is more consistent with the text description?'
Raters compare images side‑by‑side, selecting the more aesthetically pleasing image or the image more consistent with the text description.

For aesthetics, the rater is asked 'Which image do you personally prefer?' They are instructed to select images based on personal preference (e.g. aesthetically, stylistically, compositionally). To evaluate text-image alignment, the rater is asked 'Which image is more consistent with the text description?'
